newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-Faulding set for flat result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-Faulding set for flat result.

text.p: Australian drug manufacturer F.H. Faulding and Co Ltd is expected on Monday to report a flat 1995/96 result on last year's A$36.5 million net profit before abnormals but forecasts are for strong growth in 1996/97.
Analysts forecast a net profit of A$40-46.5 million for 1996/97, based largely on the U.S. sales potential of its recently approved Kadian sustained release morphine product.
The market reacted on Wednesday with some concern when Faulding announced it had been named as a defendent in a U.S. court case linked to a patent dispute over Kadian.

However, analysts contacted by Reuters noted there was no current injunction to delay the planned release in the U.S. next month of Kadian, which has also recently obtained approvals for distribution in Canada and the United Kingdom.
Faulding told its 1995 annual meeting that the result for 1995/96 to June 30 would not be materially different to that in 1994/95.
The median forecast in BZW's BARCEP broker survey is for a 1995/96 net profit before abnormals of A$36.5 million, with nine analysts predicting a profit range of A$33.4-A$38.6 million.

Macquarie Equities analyst Simon Jones, who forecasts A$36.5 million, said Faulding could surprise the market "a little bit on the upside" through the recent release in the U.S. of the Voltaren non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug.
"I don't expect they will break even (in their U.S. operations) but it could push them a bit closer," he said.
The market was looking for strong growth in the company's health care division and in injectible sales to Asia and Europe, he said.
Jones said he was predicting a A$46.5 million net profit for 1996/97, driven mostly by the U.S. prospects for Kadian.
An analyst who did not want to be named predicted A$35.2 million for 1995/96, a flat result due mainly to continuing losses from the U.S. subsidiary Faulding Inc.

"Going forward I would be looking for a lot stronger earnings growth driven by the morphine products being launched in the U.S., U.K. and Canada ... and I think they will do more than A$40 million profit, possibly the A$45 million level," the analyst said.
